questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: That it would be a fun and new place to be.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: On a social level it was perfect, but the university course was not so great.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Easy, just common sense, everything todo with university was explained on a set day.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: A explanation about courses and sign up was given by the university. work very well.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was pretty easy, we rented an apartment together a few studens from KU, and it worked great. Our landlord was very odd, so i will not link to his housing. but I found the housing on another students report from Prague.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: There are so much housing for Erasmus students in central Prague, it does not look perfect but it is worth it and not to expensive. but beware of scammers.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: A bit confusing, if you want to take courses at different faculties, you have to register at different times at the faculties because the registration does not happen at the same time for the faculties.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Register in there student information system, and if the course you want is full, write the professor a email and he will mabye let you into the course.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There where a meeting before the registration begun, where all the information was given. But you can always write your student coordinator.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: All course at, my main faculty(math and physics) were easy, but some of the courses I wanted at different faculties I did not get because I did not sign up at the right time and the course were full.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Write emails to the professors of the course you want, in good time, if it is not your main faculty. else just sign up.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It seemed very messy, the information about the course are spread across multiple websites/services(like Teams) depending on what the professor of the course likes. ¨

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
I only took one masters course on accident(Software architecture) and that was a good course not to much work. 
But in general the courses amount of work did not correspond to the points. 
It seems like i worked way to hard on the 5 ECTS point courses, to many assignments. but the exams were for the most part okay.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: You basically had to figure a lot out by yourself, but the lectures were good.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Programming and data processing in Python
Introduction to Language Technologies
Introduction to Computer Graphics
Introduction to Colour Science
Data Formats
Software System Architectures
Programming of Web Applications

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Programming and data processing in Python - fun assignments
Introduction to Language Technologies - good overall course, not to much work and sone decently fun assignments.  
Software System Architectures - if you find a good group this course is nice, 2 presentations and an exam. but it is a masters course. 
The rest of the courses it took were to much work for the points, meaning to many assignments. 
But the professor in Introduction to Computer Graphics and Introduction to Colour Science is very nice and very passionate.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Not really anything, it is very cheap to live and go out in Prague.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: A gym membership was a bit more expensive that I expected but still not to bad.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A lot of stuff, though the ESN app.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Go outside Prague 1 and 2.
Have multiple walks around Prague and just see take in the city, not just the touristy places!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: spend some weekends traveling to other cities like Bratislava and Vienna.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Not very hard.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I mostly meet other exchange students and i think that is the best things to do, because all the exchange students also wanna meet new people!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer:
People don't smile that much, and they look at you weirdly if you smile to them. 
When you go out make sure to have some cash, the really cheap bares are mostly cash only!

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: There were no single part i would say, it is not to different.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Pick courses from different faculty at least if you are going to study computer science(datalogi), otherwise there is going to be a lot of assignments. at least for the courses I picked.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Think about what you want your exchange to be about.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer:
Meeting a lot of new people.
living in the center of such a beautiful city.
Getting to know a different city so well.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I had all my exams in spread out over January, that was the hardest part of my stay.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
